# Pitloom's catalogued messages: Wheels

See also: `messages.md` (the index of every code), `../SKILL.md` (which holds
the rule: explain and relay, never run the fix).

Trust a code only when the line is one of the lines below, a value in place of

### `archive-member-conflict`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: Archive members collide where they install: a later member has the
  same install name (read with \ as a separator, as an installer on Windows
  reads it), so an installer extracting in order keeps only the later one; a
  file member's name is also a directory of other members, and no installer can
  write both; or, in an sdist, members inside and outside its top directory map
  to one project path, so they would share one ID registry key.
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: Left the member out of the SBOM (not listed); on the
  --allow-build route, did not extract it from the built wheel (not copied), so
  no file of the SBOM comes from it. The archive is not changed: an embed
  rewrites the wheel with every member it had. Members sharing a project path
  are all listed, under that path; an ID registry would give them one id.
- **Tell the user**: which members collide, as the line says; a conforming build
  tool does not write such an archive. If the archive is theirs, they rebuild it
  with a conforming build tool; else they ask whoever published it. Do not
  repack the archive for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it
  only.
- **Printed after**: `Build: <text>` (--allow-build: the build and its temporary
  directories), on its WARNING lines; the prefix is not part of the line.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': overwritten by later entry '<later-member>'; not listed [archive-member-conflict]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': overwritten by later entry '<later-member>'; not copied [archive-member-conflict]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': also a directory of other entries; not listed [archive-member-conflict]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': also a directory of other entries; not copied [archive-member-conflict]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>': members share a project path (<project-paths>); they would share one ID registry key [archive-member-conflict]
  ```

### `archive-member-invalid`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: An archive member is stored under a name that is not its install
  name (a backslash separator, an empty or '.' segment, a ./ in a wheel), so it
  is listed under the name an installer writes it to; or a member named as a
  directory (ending in /) carries bytes, which no installer writes.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Listed a non-conforming member under its install name (on the
  --allow-build route, copied it there), as the line says. Left a directory
  entry's bytes out (not listed, not copied). The archive is not changed.
- **Tell the user**: what the line says only if they asked about the archive's
  members: the SBOM names each file as it installs. If the archive is theirs,
  they rebuild it with a conforming build tool; else they ask whoever published
  it. Do not repack the archive for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask,
  report it only.
- **Printed after**: `Build: <text>` (--allow-build: the build and its temporary
  directories), on its WARNING lines; the prefix is not part of the line.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': non-conforming name; listed as '<install-name>' [archive-member-invalid]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': non-conforming name; copied as '<install-name>' [archive-member-invalid]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': directory entry carries data; not listed [archive-member-invalid]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': directory entry carries data; not copied [archive-member-invalid]
  ```

### `archive-member-unsafe`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: An archive member's name has no install location an installer could
  write it to: absolute (a leading / or a drive such as C:), with a '..'
  segment, holding a NUL, or empty once normalised; or, on the --allow-build
  route, it resolves outside the directory Pitloom extracts the built wheel into
  (a link on the way).
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: Left the member out of the SBOM (not listed); on the
  --allow-build route, did not extract it from the built wheel (not copied), so
  no file of the SBOM comes from it. The archive is not changed: an embed
  rewrites the wheel with every member it had.
- **Tell the user**: which member was left out and why, as the line says: such a
  name can write outside an install directory, and a conforming build tool does
  not write one. If the archive is theirs, they rebuild it with a conforming
  build tool; else they ask whoever published it. Do not repack the archive for
  them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Printed after**: `Build: <text>` (--allow-build: the build and its temporary
  directories), on its WARNING lines; the prefix is not part of the line.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': no safe install location; not listed [archive-member-unsafe]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': no safe install location; not copied [archive-member-unsafe]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': resolves outside the extraction directory; not copied [archive-member-unsafe]
  ```

### `dist-info-ambiguous`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A wheel has several top-level .dist-info directories and its file
  name does not pick one: several match the name and version it names (PEP 503
  names, PEP 440 versions), the file name is not a PEP 427 wheel name, or none
  matches it. Pitloom does not guess which is the wheel's own.
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: As an ERROR (verify-wheel, validate-wheel, embed-wheel, wheel
  --embed), refused the wheel: nothing is written or changed, the command exits
  1 and the library raises WheelRefused, a ValueError carrying the code. As a
  WARNING (loom wheel, generate of a wheel), wrote the SBOM with the wheel's
  files and no name, version or other METADATA of the package (named unknown).
- **Tell the user**: Pitloom cannot tell the wheel's own .dist-info, as the line
  says. They rebuild the wheel with a conforming build tool, or rename the file
  to the PEP 427 name of its own .dist-info directory, and run again. Do not
  rename or repack the wheel for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report
  it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: ARCHIVE='<archive>': several top-level .dist-info directories match the file name; wheel refused [dist-info-ambiguous]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>': several top-level .dist-info directories match the file name; identity unknown [dist-info-ambiguous]
  ERROR: ARCHIVE='<archive>': the file name is not a wheel name and several top-level .dist-info directories exist; wheel refused [dist-info-ambiguous]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>': the file name is not a wheel name and several top-level .dist-info directories exist; identity unknown [dist-info-ambiguous]
  ERROR: ARCHIVE='<archive>': several top-level .dist-info directories, none the one the file name names; wheel refused [dist-info-ambiguous]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>': several top-level .dist-info directories, none the one the file name names; identity unknown [dist-info-ambiguous]
  ```

### `dist-info-conflict`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: A wheel's PEP 427 file name names a package and version whose
  .dist-info directory the wheel does not hold; it holds exactly one other
  top-level .dist-info, which Pitloom reads as the wheel's own (a renamed file,
  or a wheel built under another name).
- **SBOM effect**: weaker: what the SBOM says is less sure.
- **Pitloom did**: Read the one .dist-info the line names as the wheel's own;
  the command goes on and its exit status does not change.
- **Tell the user**: the file name and the wheel's metadata disagree, as the
  line says. If the file was renamed, they give it back its PEP 427 name; else
  they rebuild the wheel. Do not rename it for them; ask first, and with nobody
  to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>': the file name names no top-level .dist-info; using '<member>' [dist-info-conflict]
  ```

### `dist-info-missing`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A wheel has no top-level .dist-info directory (one vendored under a
  package is never the wheel's own), or its own .dist-info has no METADATA
  member (the line names the member looked for). A conforming wheel has both.
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: As an ERROR (verify-wheel, validate-wheel, embed-wheel, wheel
  --embed), refused the wheel: nothing is written or changed, the command exits
  1 and the library raises WheelRefused, a ValueError carrying the code. As a
  WARNING (loom wheel, generate of a wheel), wrote the SBOM with the wheel's
  files and no name, version or other METADATA of the package (named unknown).
- **Tell the user**: the wheel lacks the metadata a wheel must carry, as the
  line says. They rebuild the wheel with a conforming build tool, or rename the
  file to the PEP 427 name of its own .dist-info directory, and run again. Do
  not rename or repack the wheel for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask,
  report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: ARCHIVE='<archive>': no top-level .dist-info directory; wheel refused [dist-info-missing]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>': no top-level .dist-info directory; identity unknown [dist-info-missing]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': not in the wheel; identity unknown [dist-info-missing]
  ```

### `wheel-invalid`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A wheel's member names do not let an installer tell its files
  apart: two members have one name, exactly or once read as an installer on
  Windows reads it (a/M and a\M), or a name holds a NUL, where Python's zipfile
  cuts the name, so the member installs under a shorter name that may be another
  member's. No reader can tell which member is meant.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Refused the wheel as a whole: no SBOM is written and no wheel
  is changed; the command exits 1 (a batch goes on with the next wheel and exits
  1 at the end), and the library raises WheelRefused, a ValueError carrying the
  code. The model scan of a wheel lists no file of it.
- **Tell the user**: the wheel's member names collide, as the line says; a
  conforming build tool does not write such a wheel. They rebuild the wheel with
  a conforming build tool, or ask whoever published it for a good copy, and run
  again. Do not repair or rename the wheel's members for them; ask first, and
  with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': NUL in member name; wheel refused [wheel-invalid]
  ERROR: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': duplicate member name; wheel refused [wheel-invalid]
  ```

### `wheel-unreadable`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A wheel could not be read: the file is not a ZIP archive Python can
  open (damaged, cut short, another format named .whl, a member name flagged
  UTF-8 that is not), or one of its members could not be read (damaged,
  encrypted, a compression Python cannot read, a RECORD that is not UTF-8). The
  line names the exception's type only, never its text, which quotes member
  names.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Refused the wheel as a whole: no SBOM is written and no wheel
  is changed; the command exits 1 (a batch goes on with the next wheel and exits
  1 at the end), and the library raises WheelRefused, a ValueError carrying the
  code. The model scan of a wheel lists no file of it.
- **Tell the user**: the wheel is damaged, as the line says. They rebuild the
  wheel with a conforming build tool, or ask whoever published it for a good
  copy, and run again. Do not repair or rename the wheel's members for them; ask
  first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: ARCHIVE='<archive>': could not open as a ZIP archive (<exception-type>); wheel refused [wheel-unreadable]
  ERROR: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': could not read (<exception-type>); wheel refused [wheel-unreadable]
  ```

### `wheel-unusable`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A wheel to embed an SBOM in stores a member of its own .dist-info
  directory under a name that is not its install name (a backslash, a ./ or an
  empty segment): the embed rewrites RECORD by install name, so it could not
  tell which entry it rewrites. Only an embed refuses it ('embed-wheel', 'wheel
  --embed'); a read lists the member under its install name.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Refused the wheel as a whole: no SBOM is written and no wheel
  is changed; the command exits 1 (a batch goes on with the next wheel and exits
  1 at the end), and the library raises WheelRefused, a ValueError carrying the
  code. The model scan of a wheel lists no file of it.
- **Tell the user**: the wheel cannot take an SBOM, as the line says. They
  rebuild the wheel with a conforming build tool, or ask whoever published it
  for a good copy, and run again. Do not repair or rename the wheel's members
  for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': .dist-info member under a non-conforming name; wheel refused [wheel-unusable]
  ```

### `wheel-unusable/signed`

- **Level**: ERROR, INFO. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A wheel to embed an SBOM in carries a signature of its RECORD
  (RECORD.jws or RECORD.p7s, PEP 427). The embed rewrites RECORD, so the
  signature would no longer verify. The ERROR line names --allow-signed-wheel on
  the command line, allow_signed_wheel=True in the library. As an INFO line, it
  was given and the embed removed the signature.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: As an ERROR, refused the wheel: no wheel is changed, the
  command exits 1 and the library raises WheelRefused, a ValueError carrying the
  code. As an INFO line, embedded the SBOM, rewrote RECORD and removed the
  signature: the wheel is unsigned.
- **Tell the user**: the wheel is signed and an embed would break the signature,
  as the line says. Only with their say: run again with --allow-signed-wheel
  (allow_signed_wheel=True in the library), which removes the signature, then
  they re-sign the wheel with their own key; after an INFO line, they re-sign it
  before publishing. Do not pass --allow-signed-wheel or sign for them; ask
  first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': signs the RECORD the embed rewrites; <option> removes it (re-sign the wheel after); wheel refused [wheel-unusable/signed]
  INFO: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': signature removed; re-sign the wheel [wheel-unusable/signed]
  ```
